conviction_note: The Q3 bar sits at the top of the company's own guide, and that guide already builds in a fall in GMV growth from 44% to about 34%. The two public cross-border readings since August (Mastercard card-not-present 20% to 15%, Shopify international 37% to 32%) slowed by less than that, and this name has bought its last two beat-and-raise prints. So the lean is slightly up: p_up 54 on an abs move of 13 (the option-implied 13.7%) gives +1.04. The findings sum (+0.3) is smaller because most of the negatives are small proxies that land inside the guide. The two numbers agree in sign, the guide is what decides it, and Q4 holiday data is not visible yet.
bar: Q3 revenue: company guide $308.5-315.5M; GMV guide $1.995-2.045B; adj EBITDA guide $58.5-62.5M (Q2 2026 release, https://www.taiwannews.com.tw/en/news/6419941, 2026-08-12). Consensus revenue about $314.8M, EPS $0.33, whisper $0.35 (Earnings Whispers preview, https://finviz.com/news/420673/global-e-faces-a-high-bar-as-passport-lifts-growth-and-margins-draw-scrutiny, 2026-11-10). Benzinga has about $313.0M and EPS $0.30 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/GLBE/charts). Chartmill's $319M / $0.23 is an outlier. Two estimate sources agree within 0.6% and sit at the top of the guide, so the bar is sourced. The full-year guide is GMV $8.81-9.11B, revenue $1.305-1.355B, adj EBITDA $278-300M, and FY revenue consensus is about $1.34B (TIKR, https://www.tikr.com/blog/what-shopifys-earnings-miss-tells-us-about-global-es-report-this-month). The implied Q4 GMV is about $2.96-3.26B, roughly +25% to +38% against Q4 2025's $2.36B.

findings.finding: The Q3 guide already builds in a sharp slowdown. Its GMV midpoint of $2.02B is +34% y/y against Q2's +44% ($2.089B), and -3% sequential against Q2, where Q3 2025 was about +4% sequential on Q2 2025. Management put this down to no FX tailwind and Q2 promotions normalising. Global-e has landed at or above the top of its guide in recent quarters: Q4 2025 at or above the top on every metric; Q2 2026 a beat and raise. A GMV print near or above $2.045B and revenue just above $315.5M is the base case. Revenue consensus of $314.8M sits at the top of the range, so the print needs to clear the top to count as a beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline history is empty (no 6-K read). From press: Q4 2025 at/above the top of the guide with a FY guide above consensus, stock +12% to +17% on 2026-02-18 (https://www.tikr.com/blog/global-e-stock-surges-17-on-q4-earnings-beat-is-2026-revenue-above-1-2-billion-achievable). Q2 2026 beat and raise, stock +5% to +10% intraday on 2026-08-12. Q1 2026 beat and raise, roughly flat (unverified). Q3 2025 shares up pre-bell, stock +11% in Nov 2025 (https://www.fool.com/investing/2025/12/03/why-global-e-stock-jumped-11-in-november).
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus sits at the top of the guide rather than above it, which would be visible if the street had extrapolated Q2's run rate. A modelled run-rate beat would show up as estimates well above $315.5M, and Chartmill's $319M is the only one that is. The stock is also 5% below its Nov 9 close going in.
findings.independence: The finviz/Earnings Whispers preview of 2026-11-10 (https://finviz.com/news/420673/global-e-faces-a-high-bar-as-passport-lifts-growth-and-margins-draw-scrutiny) says only a print above the range extends the pattern. It agrees on the bar, not on the outcome. The second-quarter GMV +44% and sequential math come from the same company release.

findings.finding: Mastercard's Q3 2026 cross-border card-not-present volume ex-travel grew 15%, against 20% in Q2 2026 and 21% in Q3 2025. Management cited a new EU customs fee, the timing of large retail promotions and lower crypto purchases. Its higher-yielding non-intra-Europe cross-border volume was called stable (+12% vs +13%). This is a broad public series for cross-border e-commerce in the quarter Global-e reports. A 5-point slowdown is still smaller than the 10-point GMV slowdown Global-e itself guided.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No record of GLBE reacting to payment-network cross-border data. GLBE's own GMV line has moved the stock on prints (see the guide finding).
findings.why_not_priced: Public since Oct 29-30. GLBE went on to a 2026 closing high on Nov 9 afterwards, so the market did not read it as a GLBE negative. If it had, GLBE would have fallen with the release rather than rallied, and skew would be put-bid rather than call-bid. Largely inside the company guide.
findings.independence: Proxy. Same direction as Shopify's international GMV slowdown (https://ppc.land/shopify-revenue-gains-32-to-3-7bn-as-ai-referred-orders-rise-3-3x/), a different source. Mastercard's 'EU customs fee' cause is the same fact as the EU €3 duty finding, which is sized separately and kept tiny.

findings.finding: Shopify, Global-e's dominant channel partner through Managed Markets, reported Q3 2026 on Nov 3: GMV +29.5% to $119.1B, about 0.8% below the ~$120.1B expected; international GMV +32% against +37% in Q2; Europe +33% against +34%. The stock fell about 7-10%. This is a direct counterparty reporting after Global-e last spoke, and it shows international merchant volume slowing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history of GLBE reacting to Shopify's international GMV line found. GLBE closed at $41.38 on Nov 3 and $42.49 on Nov 9, so it rose after Shopify's miss.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for two weeks, and GLBE rose after it, so the market treated it as not transmitting. Global-e's Q2 GMV grew 44% against Shopify's 32%, and the gap is new merchants. A 5-point international slowdown at Shopify maps to Global-e's same-store component only. Sized small for that reason.
findings.independence: TIKR (https://www.tikr.com/blog/what-shopifys-earnings-miss-tells-us-about-global-es-report-this-month, 2026-11-04) gives the GMV miss, $119.1B against $120.1B. Same Shopify release as the Shopify Q4 guide finding; it counts once per line.

findings.finding: Shopify guided Q4 2026 revenue growth to the low thirties, against analysts' roughly 30%, including less than one point of FX headwind. Its marketing spend is up ahead of BFCM. A channel partner signalling holiday-quarter volume above the street points the same way as a Global-e Q4 guide that holds or lifts its implied +25% to +38% Q4 GMV.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: GLBE's guidance raises have been bought: +12-17% (Feb 2026, FY guide above consensus) and +5-10% (Aug 2026, FY raised).
findings.why_not_priced: GLBE's FY revenue consensus of $1.34B is just above its guide midpoint ($1.33B), so the street has not lifted Q4 on Shopify's guide. If it had, consensus would sit at or above the top of the FY range ($1.355B).
findings.independence: Q4 detail confirmed by ppc.land (https://ppc.land/shopify-revenue-gains-32-to-3-7bn-as-ai-referred-orders-rise-3-3x/). Same Shopify release as the Shopify Q3 international finding, so it is not an independent document.

findings.finding: The euro entered Q3 2026 at about $1.14, near a one-year low after a 2% drop in June. Scattered readings put the Q3 average around 1.15-1.16, below Q3 2025. Global-e said its back-half guide assumes no FX tailwind, after Q1-Q2 had one. A slightly weaker euro against the dollar is a small headwind to dollar-reported GMV from European shoppers and to US merchants' pricing abroad, and it is roughly what the guide assumed.
findings.why_not_priced: Inside the guide's 'no FX tailwind' assumption, so it is mostly expected. Filed for completeness as a macro-to-company inference.
findings.independence: Proxy. ECB reference rate 1.1383 on 2026-07-01 (https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/exchange/eurofxref/shared/pdf/2026/07/20260701.pdf). The company's no-FX-tailwind statement is from the Q2 call summary, found via search and not fetched.

findings.finding: The EU's flat €3 customs duty on e-commerce parcels under €150 from outside the EU took effect on 1 July 2026, under Council Regulation (EU) 2026/382. It applies to US, UK and other non-EU merchants shipping into the EU, a core Global-e corridor. Mastercard cited a 'new EU customs fee' for slower cross-border volume. Global-e's Q3 guide was issued on Aug 12, six weeks after the duty took effect.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In 2025 management called the US de minimis removal a minimal impact, and as a merchant of record complexity can favour the company. No record of the stock reacting to duty changes on a print.
findings.why_not_priced: Inside the company guide, which was given after the duty took effect. Its sign for a merchant of record is ambiguous (volume headwind against the complexity tailwind).
findings.independence: Overlaps the Mastercard finding's stated cause (https://www.fxcintel.com/research/analysis/ct-mastercard-q3-2026-earnings). Kept tiny to avoid counting it twice.

findings.finding: Global-e changed its Chief Revenue Officer on 1 Oct 2026. Ran Fridman, CRO for more than five years, left; Tomer Gold (EVP SMB & Channel) succeeded him. No reason was given. A commercial-leadership turnover in Q4 can draw call questions on the enterprise pipeline and holiday launches.
findings.why_not_priced: Announced in October with no visible price reaction. It matters only if the call ties it to pipeline slippage, which nothing found suggests. Promoting from the channel side is consistent with a Shopify-heavy SMB motion.

findings.finding: Passport, acquired in 2026, is guided at Q3 revenue $24-26M on GMV of about $20M, adj EBITDA under $1M and a mid-30s gross margin. Q2 non-GAAP gross margin had already fallen to 45.3% from 46.5% a year earlier. The Q3 print will show more blended gross-margin dilution and a larger revenue-growth gap over organic. The preview names margin quality and organic growth as the scrutiny points.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026's gross-margin dip to 45.3% came with a +5-10% reaction, so it was not punished.
findings.why_not_priced: Inside the company guide and well known. Sized toward 0.
findings.independence: The finviz/Earnings Whispers preview (https://finviz.com/news/420673/global-e-faces-a-high-bar-as-passport-lifts-growth-and-margins-draw-scrutiny) flags the same margin and organic-growth scrutiny. The guide finding cites the same company release.

findings.finding: LVMH's Q3 2026 organic growth slowed to about 1%, with Fashion & Leather Goods -5% in Q3. The slowdown was driven by China, with the US, Europe and Japan growing well. Global-e carries luxury and fashion merchants but little China exposure, so the transmission is weak.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for five weeks. A distant proxy; the regions that matter to Global-e grew.

findings.finding: Global-e completed its $200M 2025 buyback in Q2 2026 ($127M in H1, including $68M in Q2) and authorised a new $500M programme on June 4, 2026. That is about 7% of a market cap near $6.8B. Q3 repurchases will be disclosed in the print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None found; buybacks rode along with positive prints.
findings.why_not_priced: The authorisation is public. Only the pace of Q3 execution is new.
findings.independence: Same company release as the guide finding.

baseline_tension: The findings lean slightly up, which agrees with the mildly call-bid skew (-3.31) and the record of beat-and-raise prints being bought. The two counterparty slowdowns (Mastercard, Shopify) cut against it and keep p_up near 50, and the -4.3% five-day drawdown is unexplained and is not counted as evidence either way.
lessons_applied: Core table / LESSONS 6 (finding inside what the company guided): Mastercard cross-border slowdown -1.0 to -0.6; it is smaller than the slowdown the Q3 guide already builds in.
Same rule: EU €3 duty -0.2 to -0.1 (in force six weeks before the guide was issued); Passport margin dilution -0.2 to -0.1 (explicitly guided).
LESSONS 5 (proxy vs a direct counterparty): Shopify Q3 international -0.5 to -0.4 net of Global-e's new-merchant growth gap (LESSONS 9); LVMH -0.2 to -0.1 (China-driven, Global-e regions grew).
LESSONS 1/7: reaction history on beat-and-raise has been bought and skew is call-bid, so the guide finding stays at +1.5; p_up 53 to 54 because the negatives inside the guide move toward 50.
LESSONS 6 (verify the bar): bar confirmed by the company guide plus two agreeing estimate sources; no cap applied.
LESSONS 8: abs_move_pct kept at 13 (option-implied 13.7, prints moved +5 to +17), not shrunk.
